name: Voice maxxing

lead: Voice-maxxing is the looksmaxxing practice of changing how one sounds, most often aiming for a deeper, more resonant voice. Looksmax.org has long-running threads on whether a deep voice raises attractiveness and how to acquire one.

Speech-language pathologists use voice therapy to alter pitch, resonance and voice quality for medical and gender-voice purposes, but no published trial has tested it as an attractiveness intervention.

paras: Voice pitch is set largely by vocal fold length and tension, with typical adult male speech around 90 to 155 Hz and female around 165 to 255 Hz. Therapy approaches work on breathing, resonance and pitch habits rather than the anatomy itself.

Training itself is low risk when taught by a clinician; forceful pitch-lowering can strain the voice, and therapy sources emphasise vocal hygiene. Surgical or hormonal changes to the voice are separate medical topics.

lead: Voice-maxxing refers to deliberate changes to pitch, resonance, and speaking style, usually to sound deeper or more masculine, in order to be perceived as more attractive or authoritative. It is a common subtopic on looksmax.org, where threads ask whether a deep voice increases attractiveness and how much [1][2].

Typical adult male speech has a fundamental frequency of about 90 to 155 Hz and typical adult female speech about 165 to 255 Hz [3]. Voice therapy, delivered by speech-language pathologists, uses techniques such as resonant voice therapy to change vocal quality, and is used in transgender voice care, voice disorders and vocal hygiene [4].

paras: Voice-maxxing discussions centre on pitch and on resonance, the sense of where the voice vibrates in the chest or face. Clinical sources describe resonant voice as felt higher and more forward in the mouth and face, and this is a common target in feminising voice work [4]. Masculinising work in the opposite direction is discussed in forums as chest resonance.

Voice therapy orientations are described as symptomatic, physiologic, hygienic, psychogenic or eclectic, with the point that no single method suits everyone [4]. Techniques include the Accent Method, chant-talk, resonant voice therapy and range-expansion exercises [4]. Hormone therapy and some surgeries change appearance more than pitch, which is why voice work is used alongside them in gender-affirming care [4].

Published trials of voice training aimed at increasing attractiveness have not been identified, and the effect of a deeper voice on attractiveness is argued in forums rather than settled by the sources reviewed here.

Threads include a voice-maxxing guide, questions such as whether a deep voice is a good halo or noticeable at all, and opposing posts claiming women prefer higher-pitched voices [1][2][5]. Titles show members debating both the size and the direction of the effect.
No studies found on voice-maxxing for attractiveness. Voice therapy has been studied clinically for medical and gender-voice purposes, but those studies are outside this entry's scope.
